# Gota Framework

> Gota is a pragmatic Go (1.27+) web framework built around the REPR (Request-Endpoint-Response) design pattern on top of `net/http`, `go-chi/chi/v5`, and `go-playground/validator/v10`. It provides typed request binding and validation, automatic OpenAPI 3.1 specification generation, interactive Scalar API documentation, and zero-dependency TypeScript client SDK code generation.

## Installation

Requires Go 1.27 or newer.

```bash
go get github.com/carlosxfelipe/gota
```

Primary packages:
- `github.com/carlosxfelipe/gota` — Top-level entry point (`gota.New`, `gota.App`, `gota.Config` aliases for `repr`, plus `gota.TypeScriptSpec`, `gota.GenerateTypeScriptSDK`, `gota.ExportTypeScriptSDK`, `gota.CheckTypeScriptSDK`, and `gota.RunCodegen` bridging `repr` and `typescript`).
- `github.com/carlosxfelipe/gota/repr` — Core REPR router, endpoint helpers, request binding, validation, errors, streaming, OpenAPI, and security auditing.
- `github.com/carlosxfelipe/gota/scalar` — Standalone or integrated Scalar API Reference UI handler, themes, SRI, and CSP configuration (not re-exported by `gota`; import directly when setting `Config.Scalar` or `scalar.Theme*`).
- `github.com/carlosxfelipe/gota/typescript` — Standalone, `repr`-independent TypeScript client SDK generator (`typescript.Spec`, `typescript.Generate`, `typescript.Export`, `typescript.Check`, `typescript.RunCodegen`).

> **Imports note:** Go does not have wildcard imports (`import *`), so each subpackage you reference directly must be imported by its path. Use `gota` alone when you only need `gota.New`, `gota.Config`, `gota.App`, or the `gota.*TypeScriptSDK` / `gota.RunCodegen` helpers (such as in a dedicated codegen entrypoint); import `repr` for route builders/helpers (`repr.Get`, `repr.Context`, HTTP error helpers), `scalar` for `scalar.Config` / `scalar.Theme*`, and `typescript` only when using the generator standalone without `repr`.

## Quick Start

```go
package main

import (
	"log"
	"net/http"

	"github.com/carlosxfelipe/gota"
	"github.com/carlosxfelipe/gota/repr"
	"github.com/carlosxfelipe/gota/scalar"
	"github.com/go-chi/chi/v5/middleware"
)

type GetUserRequest struct {
	ID string `param:"id" doc:"User ID" example:"usr_1" validate:"required"`
}

type UserResponse struct {
	ID   string `json:"id" example:"usr_1"`
	Name string `json:"name" example:"Ada Lovelace"`
}

func main() {
	app := gota.New(gota.Config{
		Title:                 "My API",
		Version:               "1.0.0",
		Description:           "Example Gota service.",
		DisallowUnknownFields: true,
		Scalar: scalar.Config{
			Theme:  scalar.ThemeFastify,
			Layout: "classic",
		},
	})

	app.Use(middleware.RequestID, middleware.Logger, middleware.Recoverer)

	repr.Get(app, "/users/{id}", func(ctx *repr.Context, req GetUserRequest) (UserResponse, error) {
		return UserResponse{ID: req.ID, Name: "Ada Lovelace"}, nil
	}).
		Summary("Get user by ID").
		Tags("Users").
		ErrorResponse(http.StatusNotFound, "User not found")

	if err := app.ListenGraceful(":3000"); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```

## Configuration (`repr.Config`)

`gota.New(cfg)` / `repr.New(cfg)` accepts `repr.Config`:

- `Title` (`string`, default `"API Reference"`): OpenAPI `info.title`, Scalar page title (when `Scalar.Title` is empty), and TypeScript SDK header comment (via `gota.TypeScriptSpec`).
- `Version` (`string`, default `"1.0.0"`): OpenAPI `info.version` and TypeScript SDK header comment.
- `Description` (`string`): OpenAPI `info.description` and TypeScript SDK header comment.
- `DocsURL` (`string`, default `"/docs"`): Scalar UI route.
- `OpenAPIURL` (`string`, default `"/openapi.json"`): OpenAPI 3.1 JSON spec route.
- `DisableDocs` (`bool`): Disables `/docs` and `/openapi.json` routes.
- `Scalar` (`scalar.Config`): Visual and security settings for Scalar UI.
- `Servers` (`[]repr.OpenAPIServer`): OpenAPI `servers` entries.
- `SecuritySchemes` (`map[string]repr.OpenAPISecurityScheme`): OpenAPI `components.securitySchemes`.
- `DocsMiddlewares` (`[]func(http.Handler) http.Handler`): Middlewares applied ONLY to docs and OpenAPI routes (e.g. `middleware.BasicAuth`). Docs routes run on an isolated router (`docsMux`) and do not inherit `app.Use(...)` middlewares such as CORS.
- `MaxBodyBytes` (`int64`, default `10 MiB`): Max request body read limit.
- `MaxMultipartMemory` (`int64`, default `32 MiB`): Max memory for `ParseMultipartForm`.
- `MaxHeaderBytes` (`int`, default `1 MiB`), `ReadTimeout` (`30s`), `WriteTimeout` (`30s`), `IdleTimeout` (`120s`): HTTP server limits (negative timeout disables that timeout).
- `DisallowUnknownFields` (`bool`): Rejects unknown fields when decoding JSON request bodies.
- `SilenceTagWarnings` (`bool`): Suppresses security log warnings during OpenAPI spec and TypeScript SDK generation for sensitive field names without `json:"-"` or `form:"-"`.

## Server Lifecycle

- `app.Listen(addr)`: Starts `http.Server` (accepts `":3000"`, `"3000"`, or `"host:3000"`).
- `app.ListenGraceful(addr, shutdownTimeout...)`: Starts the server and gracefully shuts down on `SIGINT` / `SIGTERM` (default shutdown timeout: `10s`).
- `app.ServeHTTP(w, r)`: `App` implements `http.Handler` for custom server wiring or `httptest`.
- `app.Router() *chi.Mux`: Exposes the underlying chi router.
- `app.Config() repr.Config` / `app.Routes() []*repr.Route`: Read-only accessors for registered configuration and routes (`rt.Method()`, `rt.Path()`, `rt.Doc()`).

## Defining Endpoints

### 1. Function-Based REPR Endpoints

Register typed handlers with `repr.Get`, `repr.Post`, `repr.Put`, `repr.Patch`, or `repr.Delete`:

```go
repr.Post(app, "/todos", func(ctx *repr.Context, req CreateTodoRequest) (TodoResponse, error) {
	return createTodo(req), nil
}).
	Status(http.StatusCreated).
	Summary("Create a todo").
	Tags("Todos")
```

Use `repr.Empty` (or `struct{}{}`) when an endpoint has no request input or no response body. Returning `repr.Empty{}` automatically writes `204 No Content`.

### 2. Struct-Based REPR Endpoints

Implement `repr.Endpoint[Req, Res]` (`Handle(ctx *repr.Context, req Req) (Res, error)`) and register with `repr.HandleEndpoint`:

```go
type GetTodoEndpoint struct {
	Store *TodoStore
}

func (e *GetTodoEndpoint) Handle(_ *repr.Context, req GetTodoRequest) (TodoResponse, error) {
	todo, ok := e.Store.Find(req.ID)
	if !ok {
		return TodoResponse{}, repr.NotFound("Todo not found")
	}
	return todo, nil
}

repr.HandleEndpoint(app, http.MethodGet, "/todos/{id}", &GetTodoEndpoint{Store: store}).
	Summary("Get todo by ID").
	Tags("Todos").
	ErrorResponse(http.StatusNotFound, "Todo not found")
```

### 3. Non-REPR and Standard `net/http` Routes

- `app.Get`, `app.Post`, `app.Put`, `app.Patch`, `app.Delete`, `app.Route(method, path, handler)` — Register `func(ctx *repr.Context) error` handlers that expose route metadata in OpenAPI, Scalar, and SDK codegen using `.Request(...)`, `.Param(...)`, `.Response(...)`, and `.ResponseMedia(...)`.
- `app.HandleHTTP(method, path, httpHandler)` — Register a standard `http.Handler` exposed in OpenAPI, Scalar, and SDK codegen.
- `app.Handle(method, path, httpHandler)` — Register an undocumented standard `http.Handler` directly on chi.
- Non-REPR routes start with an empty `200 OK` placeholder response; calling `.Response(2xx, ...)` / `.ResponseMedia(2xx, ...)` with another `2xx` status or `.Status(code)` replaces that placeholder.

```go
app.Get("/health", func(ctx *repr.Context) error {
	return ctx.JSON(HealthStatus{Status: "ok"})
}).
	Summary("Health check").
	Tags("System").
	Response(http.StatusOK, HealthStatus{}, "Service health status")
```

## Route Metadata Builders (`*repr.Route`)

All REPR and documented non-REPR registration methods return `*repr.Route`:

- `.Summary(s)` / `.Description(d)` / `.OperationID(id)`
- `.Tags(tags...)` — Adds OpenAPI tags. All tags appear in OpenAPI; the TypeScript SDK uses the first tag as the module name (falling back to the first meaningful static path segment, or `default` when none exists). Explicit route/child-group tags take precedence ahead of parent `Group.Tags(...)`.
- `.Security(schemes...)` — Adds OpenAPI security requirements. If not explicitly defined in `Config.SecuritySchemes`, `BearerAuth`/`bearerAuth` auto-populates as HTTP Bearer (`JWT`), `BasicAuth`/`basicAuth` as HTTP Basic, and any other name defaults to HTTP Bearer.
- `.Deprecated()` / `.Hidden()` — Marks deprecated or omits from OpenAPI & TypeScript output.
- `.Status(code)` — Overrides the default `200` success status code in OpenAPI, and at runtime for REPR endpoints (unless `ctx.Status(...)` is called explicitly; non-REPR handlers must still call `ctx.Status(...)` at runtime).
- `.ErrorResponse(status, description, model...)` — Documents an error status (defaults to `repr.ErrorResponse{}`).
- `.Response(status, model, description...)` / `.ResponseMedia(status, contentType, model, description...)` — Documents responses (mainly for non-REPR routes or multiple status codes).
- `.Request(model, description...)` / `.Param(in, name, model, required, description...)` — Documents inputs on non-REPR routes (`in`: `"path"`, `"query"`, or `"header"`).

## Middlewares & Route Groups

Gota uses standard `func(http.Handler) http.Handler` middlewares and chi's ordering rule (`Use` must be called before registering routes).

```go
app.Use(middleware.RequestID, middleware.Logger, middleware.Recoverer)

api := app.Group("/api/v1").Security("BearerAuth").Tags("Account")
api.Use(authMiddleware)

repr.Get(api, "/me", getProfileHandler)

admin := api.Group("/admin", adminOnlyMiddleware).Tags("Admin")
repr.Delete(admin, "/users/{id}", deleteUserHandler)
```

- `Group` supports `Use`, `Security`, `Tags` (inherited by routes and nested subgroups; child/route tags take precedence for SDK module grouping), `Group` (nested), `Route`, `Get`, `Post`, `Put`, `Patch`, `Delete`, `HandleHTTP`, and all `repr.Get`/`Post`/`Put`/`Patch`/`Delete`/`HandleEndpoint` functions.

## Request Binding & Struct Tags

Gota binds request structs from URL path parameters, query parameters, headers, forms/multipart uploads, and JSON bodies:

| Tag | Source | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `param:"id"` | URL path param `{id}` | Required automatically. Panics at startup if `{id}` is missing from route path. Do NOT use `path:"..."`. |
| `query:"page"` | Query string | Supports slices via repeated keys (`?tag=a&tag=b`) or comma-separated values. |
| `header:"X-Api-Key"` | Request header | Bound from `r.Header.Get(...)`. |
| `form:"avatar"` | Form / Multipart | Sets OpenAPI content type to `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, or `multipart/form-data` when a field is `*multipart.FileHeader` or `[]*multipart.FileHeader`. Use `form:"-"` to ignore from binding, OpenAPI, and TypeScript. |
| `json:"title"` | JSON body | Use `json:"-"` to exclude from JSON, OpenAPI, and TypeScript. |
| `validate:"..."` | Validation rules | `go-playground/validator/v10` rules (`required`, `min=3`, `max=50`, `len=6`, `oneof=low normal high`, `email`, `url`, `uuid`, `omitempty`, `nowarn`). Reflected in OpenAPI (`minLength`, `minimum`, `enum`, `format`, `required`) and TypeScript (`oneof` on strings becomes a literal union). |
| `msg:"..."` | Custom error messages | Single message (`msg:"Todo ID is required"`) or pipe-delimited per-rule (`msg:"required:Title is required|min:Too short"`). Requires a `validate` tag. Do NOT use `message:"..."`. |
| `doc:"..."` | Description | Populates OpenAPI description and TypeScript JSDoc. |
| `example:"..."` | Example value | Typed OpenAPI example and `@example` JSDoc tag. |
| `default:"..."` | Default value | OpenAPI `default` and `@default` JSDoc tag. |
| `format:"..."` | OpenAPI format | Overrides OpenAPI `format` and `@format` JSDoc tag. |
| `deprecated:"true"` | Deprecation flag | Adds `@deprecated` in TypeScript JSDoc. |

Supported types for `param`/`query`/`header`/`form`: `string`, `int*`, `uint*`, `float*`, `bool` (`true/1/t/yes/y`, `false/0/f/no/n`), `time.Time` (`RFC3339Nano`, `RFC3339`, `2006-01-02`), addressable `encoding.TextUnmarshaler` (pointer receiver), pointers, slices (comma-separated, or repeated keys for `query`/`form`), anonymous embedded structs, plus `*multipart.FileHeader` / `[]*multipart.FileHeader` for `form`.

Security guarantee: fields tagged exclusively with `param`, `query`, `header`, or `form` (without `json`) are zeroed after JSON decoding so JSON payloads cannot spoof path/query/header fields.

Startup tag checks fail fast (panic on route registration) for common mistakes such as `path:"..."`, `message:"..."`, `msg` without `validate`, options on `param`/`query`/`header`/`form` (like `query:"id,omitempty"`), invalid `validate` tags, or `param` tags absent from the route path.

### Response Headers

Fields on a response struct tagged with `header:"X-Total-Count"` write that HTTP header on non-zero values and are documented in OpenAPI `responses.<status>.headers`.

## Validation & Error Handling

### Validation

- Automatic validation runs before the handler and returns `422 Unprocessable Entity` with `repr.ValidationError`:
  ```json
  { "message": "Validation failed", "errors": { "title": ["Title is required"] }, "status": 422 }
  ```
  Field keys in `errors` use the first non-ignored struct tag in priority order `json`, `form`, `query`, `param`, `header`, falling back to the Go field name (nested structs use dotted paths such as `"address.city"`).
- Register custom validator rules with `repr.RegisterValidation(tag, fn)`.
- Implement `repr.Validator` (`Validate() error`) or `repr.ContextValidator` (`Validate(ctx *repr.Context) error`) on request structs for cross-field validation. Returning `*repr.ValidationError` merges its `Errors` map per field; any other `error` is recorded under key `"_"`.

### Error Helpers & Custom Error Handler

Return typed HTTP errors from handlers:
- `repr.BadRequest(msg)` (400)
- `repr.Unauthorized(msg)` (401)
- `repr.Forbidden(msg)` (403)
- `repr.NotFound(msg)` (404)
- `repr.Conflict(msg)` (409)
- `repr.UnprocessableEntity(msg)` (422)
- `repr.InternalServerError(msg)` (500)
- `repr.NewHTTPError(status, msg)`

`*repr.HTTPError` renders as `repr.ErrorResponse` (`{"error": "...", "status": 404, "requestId": "..."}`). Any custom error implementing `HTTPStatus() int` is serialized directly as JSON with that HTTP status. Unhandled errors return `500`. If response headers/body were already written (`ctx.Written()`), `defaultErrorHandler` logs the error without overwriting the response. Override `app.ErrorHandler = func(ctx *repr.Context, err error) { ... }` to customize.

## Streaming & Server-Sent Events (SSE)

Return `repr.SSEStream` (or a custom `repr.Streamer` / `repr.StreamFunc`) from a REPR endpoint. When a `Streamer` is returned, Gota clears the HTTP write deadline before calling `Stream(ctx)`. `repr.SSEStream` sets OpenAPI media type to `text/event-stream` and types the TypeScript SDK response as `ReadableStream<string>`; a generic `Streamer` sets `application/octet-stream` and types the TypeScript SDK response as `Blob`. Inside `ctx.SSEvent`, each frame is written with a `10s` (`repr.DefaultSSEWriteTimeout`) deadline that is cleared again after the write. (Calling `ctx.Stream(...)` directly in a non-REPR handler does not clear the server's `WriteTimeout` automatically.)

```go
repr.Get(app, "/events", func(ctx *repr.Context, _ repr.Empty) (repr.SSEStream, error) {
	ch := make(chan repr.SSEvent)
	go func() {
		defer close(ch)
		select {
		case ch <- repr.SSEvent{Event: "update", Data: map[string]string{"status": "ready"}}:
		case <-ctx.Context().Done():
		}
	}()
	return repr.SSEStream{Events: ch}, nil
})
```

Imperative helpers on `*repr.Context`: `ctx.SSEvent(event, data)` and `ctx.Stream(func(w io.Writer) bool)`.

## `*repr.Context` Reference

- Construction & raw HTTP: `repr.NewContext(w, r)` (for unit tests), `ctx.Writer` (`http.ResponseWriter`), `ctx.Request` (`*http.Request`).
- Request info: `ctx.Context()`, `ctx.Param(name)`, `ctx.Header(key)`, `ctx.RequestID()`, `ctx.Cookie(name)`, `ctx.Body()`, `ctx.DecodeJSON(data, target)`
- Response writing: `ctx.Status(code)`, `ctx.SetHeader(key, val)`, `ctx.SetCookie(cookie)`, `ctx.JSON(data)` (sets `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`), `ctx.NoContent()` (writes `204`), `ctx.Redirect(url, code...)` (defaults to `302`), `ctx.RedirectLocal(target, code...)`, `ctx.Stream(...)`, `ctx.SSEvent(event, data)`
- State checks: `ctx.StatusCode()`, `ctx.StatusExplicit()`, `ctx.Written()`

## OpenAPI 3.1 & Scalar Docs

- OpenAPI 3.1 spec is available at `Config.OpenAPIURL` (default `/openapi.json`), programmatically via `app.OpenAPISpec()`, or exported via `app.ExportOpenAPI("openapi.json")`.
- Scalar API Reference UI is served at `Config.DocsURL` (default `/docs`) using `@scalar/api-reference` (pinned at `scalar.DefaultVersion` `"1.76.0"` with `scalar.DefaultSRI`) and security headers (`X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, and CSP).
- `scalar.Config` fields: `Title`, `SpecURL`, `Theme`, `Layout` (`"modern"` default or `"classic"`), `DarkMode *bool`, `ShowSidebar *bool`, `ProxyURL`, `CustomCSS`, `SearchHotKey`, `Metadata map[string]string`, `ScriptURL`, `SRI` (applied only when `ScriptURL` is non-empty; default CDN always uses `DefaultSRI`), `CSP` (`""` uses `scalar.ContentSecurityPolicy(ScriptURL)`; `"-"` omits the CSP header), and `CSPReportOnly` (`false` default sends enforcing `Content-Security-Policy`; `true` sends `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only`).
- Available `scalar.Theme` constants: `ThemeDefault` (default), `ThemeAlternate`, `ThemeMoon`, `ThemePurple`, `ThemeSolarized`, `ThemeBluePlanet`, `ThemeDeepSpace`, `ThemeSaturn`, `ThemeKepler`, `ThemeElysiaJS`, `ThemeFastify`, `ThemeMars`, `ThemeLaserwave`, `ThemeNone`.
- Helpers: `scalar.Handler(cfg)` (mounts standalone on `http.ServeMux` or `chi`), `scalar.RenderHTML(cfg)`, `scalar.ContentSecurityPolicy(scriptURL)`, `scalar.CDNURL(version)`.

## TypeScript SDK & Offline Codegen

`github.com/carlosxfelipe/gota/typescript` is a standalone, zero-external-dependency package that generates a modular, zero-dependency TypeScript `fetch` client (`createClient`) typed via `ApiEndpoints`. It has no dependency on `repr` and can be used with any Go router (`chi`, `net/http`, `Echo`, etc.) or bridged from a Gota `repr.App` via `gota.TypeScriptSpec(app)`.

### Using `typescript` with Gota (`gota.TypeScriptSpec`) or Standalone (`typescript.Spec`)

Generate the modular SDK during development or CI/CD via `gota.RunCodegen(app, os.Args[1:])` (or decoupled via `typescript.RunCodegen(gota.TypeScriptSpec(app), os.Args[1:])`):

```go
// With Gota / repr.App (no need to import repr or typescript):
if handled, err := gota.RunCodegen(app, os.Args[1:]); handled {
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	return
}

// Standalone (without repr, e.g., pure chi or net/http):
spec := typescript.Spec{
	Config: typescript.Config{Title: "My API", Version: "1.0.0"},
	Routes: []typescript.Route{
		{
			Method:      http.MethodPost,
			Path:        "/todos",
			Tags:        []string{"Todos"},
			RequestBody: &typescript.RequestBody{ContentType: "application/json", Required: true, Model: CreateTodoRequest{}},
			Responses:   map[int]*typescript.Response{http.StatusCreated: {ContentType: "application/json", Model: TodoResponse{}}},
		},
	},
}
_ = typescript.Export(spec, "./dist", typescript.Options{ImportExtension: "auto"})
```

Supported `RunCodegen` CLI flags:
- `--ts-sdk` (defaults to `./dist`) / `--ts-sdk=<dir>` — modular TypeScript client SDK directory (`index.ts`, `runtime.ts`, `types/<module>.ts`, `types/_shared.ts`, `endpoints/<module>.ts`)
- `--ts-import-ext=<ext>` — relative import suffix in `--ts-sdk`: `""`/`none` (default, bundlers), `".js"` (`node16`/`nodenext` ESM), `".ts"` (Node type stripping, Deno, Bun), or `"auto"` (autodetect from nearest `deno.json(c)`, `tsconfig.json`, or `package.json`)
- `--check` — CI verification mode (requires `--ts-sdk`); verifies exported SDK matches current routes (no missing, modified, or stale managed files) without writing to disk

`typescript` API: `typescript.Spec`, `typescript.Config`, `typescript.Route`, `typescript.Param`, `typescript.RequestBody`, `typescript.Response`, `typescript.Options`, `typescript.NewGenerator(cfg)`, `typescript.Generate(spec, opts...)`, `typescript.Export(spec, dir, opts...)`, `typescript.Check(spec, dir, opts...)`, `typescript.RunCodegen(spec, args)`, `typescript.DetectImportExtension(dir)`.

Root `gota` bridge helpers: `gota.TypeScriptSpec(app)`, `gota.GenerateTypeScriptSDK(app, opts...)`, `gota.ExportTypeScriptSDK(app, dir, opts...)`, `gota.CheckTypeScriptSDK(app, dir, opts...)`, `gota.RunCodegen(app, args)`.

### Modular Layout, Schema Rules & Project Extensions

Running `--ts-sdk=./src/lib/sdk` splits schemas and `ApiEndpoints` by module (`types/<module>.ts`, `types/_shared.ts`, `endpoints/<module>.ts`), using the route's first tag (inherited from `Group.Tags(...)` or set via `route.Tags(...)`) or falling back to the first meaningful static path segment (skipping leading `api` / `v[0-9]+`, falling back to `default` only for `/` or param-only paths). It isolates the route-independent core in `runtime.ts` and removes stale managed files on regeneration while preserving determinism for clean Git diffs.

Schema generation rules:
- Structs reachable only from responses use serialization semantics (fields without `omitempty`/`omitzero` are required, and pointer fields become `T | null`); structs used in requests (or shared across requests and responses) use input optionality (fields without `validate:"required"` are optional `?`).
- Struct-level JSDoc is read from `Doc() string`, `Description() string`, or `_ struct{} \`doc:"..."\``.

Keep project-specific client configuration and domain helpers in a separate wrapper outside the generated directory (e.g., `src/lib/api.ts` importing from `./sdk`), so regenerating the SDK overwrites only the generated directory. In CI, run your codegen binary with `--ts-sdk=... --check` to catch forgotten SDK updates.

### Using the Generated TypeScript SDK

Generated `index.ts` exports: `createClient`, `isEndpointError`, `ApiClient`, `ApiEndpoints`, `EndpointKey`, `RequestParams<K>`, `RequestQuery<K>`, `RequestBody<K>`, `ResponseData<K>`, `ResponseError<K>`, `RequestOptions<K>`, plus everything from `runtime.ts` (`HttpError`, `isHttpError`, `isAbortError`, `parseError`, `ApiErrorKind`, `ApiErrorDetails`, `ClientOptions`, `RetryConfig`, `RequestConfig`, `ResponseContext`, `QueryOptions`, `DEFAULT_RETRY_METHODS`, `createClientFor`).

```ts
// src/lib/api.ts (project wrapper outside the generated ./sdk directory)
import {
  createClient,
  isAbortError,
  isEndpointError,
  parseError,
} from "./sdk";

export const api = createClient(process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL ?? "http://localhost:3000", {
  headers: async () => ({ Authorization: `Bearer ${getToken()}` }),
  timeoutMs: 8000,
  retry: 2,
});

export { isAbortError, isEndpointError, parseError };
```

#### Error Parsing & Narrowing

Use `parseError(err)` instead of custom error parsers to normalize HTTP errors, Gota `ValidationError` (`kind === "validation"` with `fieldErrors`), `ErrorResponse` (`requestId`), timeouts (`kind === "timeout"`), caller cancellations (`kind === "abort"`), and network failures (`kind === "network"`):

```ts
try {
  const created = await api.fetch("POST /todos", {
    body: { title: "Ship release", priority: "high" },
  });
} catch (err) {
  if (isEndpointError(err, "POST /todos")) {
    // err.data is narrowed to ResponseError<"POST /todos">
  }
  const parsed = parseError(err);
  if (parsed.kind === "validation") {
    console.error(parsed.fieldErrors); // Record<string, string[]>
  } else {
    console.error(parsed.message, parsed.requestId);
  }
}
```

#### Frontend Hooks (TanStack Query / SWR) & Effect Cancellation

Prefer `api.queryOptions(...)` with a data-fetching library (or a thin service/hook layer) over calling `api.fetch` directly inside `useEffect`:

```ts
// TanStack Query: automatically passes { signal } and builds prefix-invalidatable keys
const todosQuery = useQuery(api.queryOptions("GET /todos", { query: { done: false } }));
// Invalidate any variant with: queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ["GET /todos"] })

// SWR:
const { queryKey, queryFn } = api.queryOptions("GET /todos", { query: { done: false } });
const { data } = useSWR(queryKey, () => queryFn());
```

When using `useEffect` directly, pass an `AbortController.signal` and ignore `isAbortError(err)` (caller cancellations also automatically skip `onError` hooks):

```ts
useEffect(() => {
  const controller = new AbortController();
  api
    .fetch("GET /todos", { query: { done: false }, signal: controller.signal })
    .then(setTodos)
    .catch((err) => {
      if (isAbortError(err)) return;
      setError(parseError(err).message);
    });
  return () => controller.abort();
}, []);
```

Client features: dynamic sync/async `headers`, `credentials`, `cache`, Next.js `next` (`revalidate` / `tags`), `timeoutMs`, `retry` (exponential backoff with `Retry-After` support on idempotent methods), `onRequest`/`onResponse`/`onError` hooks, `onUnauthorized` (runs at most once on HTTP `401` for non-stream bodies; return `true` to rebuild headers and retry once, `false` to raise the `401` `HttpError`), `AbortSignal` cancellation, `queryOptions` helper, `parseError` / `isHttpError` / `isAbortError` / `isEndpointError`, automatic `FormData` (from `FormData` or plain objects with `Blob`/`File`) and `URLSearchParams` encoding, and `ReadableStream<string>` for SSE responses.

## Security & Auditing Utilities

- **Sensitive field detection**: `repr.AuditModel(model)`, `app.AuditRoutes()`, and `repr.IsSensitiveFieldName(name)` check for exposed secret-like fields (`Password`, `PasswordHash`, `Secret`, `PrivateKey`, `AuthToken`, `CVV`, etc.) missing `json:"-"` / `form:"-"`. Use `validate:"nowarn"` on a specific field or `Config.SilenceTagWarnings: true` to suppress logs.
- **Upload filename sanitization**: `repr.SanitizeFilename(header.Filename)` strips directory traversal paths, control characters, and hidden dotfiles.
- **Safe local redirects**: `ctx.RedirectLocal(target, code...)` and `repr.IsLocalRedirectTarget(target)` reject external URLs, protocol-relative URLs (`//`), and backslashes with `400 Bad Request`.

## Modern Go Conventions (Go 1.27+)

When writing or modifying code in Gota or services built with it, follow modern Go idioms instead of legacy patterns:

- **Defaults & fallbacks**: Prefer `cmp.Or(val, fallback)` over repetitive zero-value `if` blocks (note that all arguments to `cmp.Or` are evaluated before the call, so keep an `if` when the fallback has side effects or is expensive).
- **Typed error matching**: Prefer `if e, ok := errors.AsType[*repr.HTTPError](err); ok` (and `errors.Is`) over `var e *T; errors.As(err, &e)` in custom `ErrorHandler`s and middlewares.
- **Pointer literals**: Use `new(value)` for pointer fields/arguments (e.g., `DarkMode: new(true)` in `scalar.Config` or pointer request fields) instead of temporary variables or `ptr` helpers.
- **Slices, maps & sorting**: Prefer `slices.Clone`, `slices.Concat`, `slices.Delete`, `slices.Contains`, `slices.Sort`, `slices.SortFunc` (with `cmp.Compare`), `slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(m))`, `maps.Copy`, and `clear(m)` over manual loops, `append` cloning tricks, or `sort.Slice` / `sort.Strings`.
- **Strings & loops**: Prefer `strings.SplitSeq` / `strings.FieldsSeq` when iterating over split parts, `strings.Cut` / `strings.CutPrefix` / `strings.CutSuffix` / `strings.CutLast` over `Index` + slicing, and `for i := range n` for simple zero-based count loops.
- **JSON tags & `encoding/json`**: Use `omitzero` on `bool`, numeric, struct, and `time.Time` fields whose zero value should be omitted (keeping `omitempty` for empty strings, slices, and maps). Leave existing `encoding/json` code unchanged unless migrating deliberately to `encoding/json/v2`, as wire defaults differ (e.g., nil slices/maps and stricter UTF-8/duplicate-key checks).
- **Concurrency, reflection & tests**: Prefer `wg.Go(...)` (`sync.WaitGroup.Go`), typed atomics (`atomic.Bool`, `atomic.Int64`, `atomic.Pointer[T]`), `any` over `interface{}`, `reflect.TypeFor[T]()` over `reflect.TypeOf((*T)(nil)).Elem()`, `t.Context()` in tests, and `b.Loop()` in benchmarks.
